title: Optimistic vs pessimistic locking
context: How do optimistic and pessimistic locking work with JPA and a relational database? When would you choose each one?
answer: Optimistic locking adds a @Version column. Updates include WHERE version = ? and bump it; if another transaction changed the row first, zero rows match and JPA throws OptimisticLockException, which you handle by retrying or telling the user. No locks are held while the user thinks, so it suits low contention and long workflows. Pessimistic locking takes a database row lock up front (SELECT … FOR UPDATE, LockModeType.PESSIMISTIC_WRITE), so other writers wait. It suits high contention on the same rows, like debiting a popular account, but holds locks, needs short transactions, consistent lock order to avoid deadlocks, and lock timeouts.

points.title: Optimistic: version check on update
points.why: A @Version column is compared and incremented on every update; a mismatch means someone else won.

points.title: Optimistic conflicts are handled by retrying
points.why: The losing transaction fails and must retry or report a conflict.

points.title: Pessimistic: row lock up front
points.why: SELECT … FOR UPDATE (PESSIMISTIC_WRITE) blocks other writers until commit.

points.title: Choose by contention
points.why: Low contention or long user think time: optimistic. Frequent conflicts on the same rows: pessimistic.

points.title: Pessimistic risks: deadlocks and waits
points.why: Locks must be short-lived, taken in a consistent order, and bounded by a timeout.
